c-pg-angles.label: Angle sum of a polygon
c-pg-angles.summary: The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°. In a cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles add to 180°.

q-pg-ratio.label: Angles in a given ratio
q-pg-ratio.summary: Four angles in a ratio like 1 : 3 : 4 : 4; find the largest or smallest.

c-pg-regular.label: Interior/exterior angles of a regular polygon
c-pg-regular.summary: Every exterior angle of a regular n-gon is 360°/n, and it pairs with its interior angle to 180°. The angle sum is (n−2)×180°.

q-pg-sides.label: Find n from an angle condition
q-pg-sides.summary: Given a ratio, a sum, or an interior-angle value for a regular polygon, find (or rule out) the number of sides.

c-pg-cyclic.label: Cyclic quadrilateral and trapezium facts
c-pg-cyclic.summary: A cyclic trapezium is always an isosceles trapezium, so its base angles are equal. An exterior angle of any cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior angle at the opposite vertex.

q-pg-cyclic.label: Cyclic trapezium base angles, or the exterior-angle rule
q-pg-cyclic.summary: Find a base angle of a cyclic trapezium, or the interior opposite angle from a given exterior angle.

c-pg-rhombus.label: Angles and diagonals of a rhombus
c-pg-rhombus.summary: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal and adjacent angles are supplementary. A diagonal splits it into two triangles with two equal sides (the rhombus's sides), solvable with the cosine rule.

q-pg-rhombus.label: Find a rhombus angle or diagonal
q-pg-rhombus.summary: Given one angle (or a ratio of two angles), find another angle or a diagonal's length.

formulas.text: Sum of the angles of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°
Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles add to 180°
formulas.note: Use it as a check or as the main step when two angles are given.

formulas.text: Exterior angle of a regular n-gon = 360°/n; interior + exterior = 180°; sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°
formulas.note: Any one of these, plus whatever the question gives (a ratio, a sum, a single angle), pins down n — and n must come out a whole number ≥ 3.

formulas.text: Cyclic trapezium (AD ∥ BC) is isosceles: the base angles at B and C are equal, so ∠BCD = ∠ABC directly
formulas.note: A trapezium that is also cyclic has no freedom left — it must be isosceles.

formulas.text: Exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral = interior angle at the opposite vertex
formulas.note: Not the same-vertex interior angle (that one is merely supplementary to the exterior angle).

formulas.text: Rhombus: opposite angles equal, adjacent angles supplementary; a diagonal BD in triangle ABD (sides AB = AD) gives BD² = 2·AB²·(1 − cos∠A)
formulas.note: ∠A here is the angle between the two sides meeting at the diagonal's own vertex, not the angle given at B or C — convert first with the supplementary-angles rule.

q-pg-ratio.cue: 'The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio …'; find the biggest or smallest angle.
q-pg-ratio.standard: Ratio parts add to 1 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 12. One part = 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. Largest = 4 × 30° = 120°.
q-pg-ratio.fast: 360 ÷ 12 = 30 is clean, so every angle is a multiple of 30°. Only the multiples of 30 can be an answer.
q-pg-ratio.eliminate: The largest angle's share is 4/12 = 1/3 of 360° = 120°. Options that are not multiples of 30 (108°, 135°) are out; 90° is the 3-part angle.
traps: Using 180° instead of 360° (opposite angles are 180° but the whole sum is 360°).
Picking the 3-part angle (90°) as the largest.
Pairing opposite angles and getting inconsistent ratios; the question is solved from the angle sum alone.

q-pg-sides.cue: 'The exterior and interior angles are in the ratio …', 'the sum of the interior angles is …°', or 'which of these can never be an interior angle?'
q-pg-sides.standard: Turn whatever is given into the exterior angle (or n − 2), then use n = 360°/exterior or n = sum/180° + 2.
q-pg-sides.fast: For a 'can never be' question, just check whether 180° − (the angle) divides 360° exactly — if not, that angle is impossible.
q-pg-sides.eliminate: n must be a whole number at least 3; throw out any angle or ratio that gives a fraction or a value under 3.
traps: Mixing up the interior and exterior angle in the ratio.
Forgetting the '+2' (or '−2') when going between the angle sum and n.
For the impossible-angle question, checking only one option instead of all four.

q-pg-cyclic.cue: 'ABCD is a cyclic trapezium…' asking for the other base angle, or 'an exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is …°, find the interior opposite angle'.
q-pg-cyclic.standard: For the trapezium: recognise it must be isosceles, so the two base angles on the same parallel side are equal — no further computation. For the exterior-angle question: the interior opposite angle simply equals the given exterior angle.
q-pg-cyclic.fast: Both facts are direct equalities — there is nothing to compute once the rule is recalled.
q-pg-cyclic.eliminate: 180° minus the given angle is the trap answer in both cases (confusing 'opposite' with 'same vertex', or the ordinary co-interior angle rule) — rule it out.
traps: Treating the base angles as supplementary (180° − angle) instead of equal.
Using the exterior angle = same-vertex interior angle's supplement instead of the opposite vertex's interior angle.
Forgetting that only a trapezium that is ALSO cyclic is guaranteed isosceles.

q-pg-rhombus.cue: 'ABCD is a rhombus … ∠A : ∠B = …' or '… side AB = … cm and ∠ABC = …°, find diagonal BD/AC'.
q-pg-rhombus.standard: For an angle: split 180° by the given ratio, then use equal-opposite-angles. For a diagonal: find the angle at the diagonal's own vertex (180° minus the given adjacent angle), then apply the cosine rule with the two equal sides.
q-pg-rhombus.fast: If the angle at the diagonal's vertex works out to 60°, the triangle on that diagonal is equilateral — the diagonal equals the side, no cosine rule needed.
q-pg-rhombus.eliminate: The diagonal must be less than twice the side and (for angle < 180°) more than 0; options far outside that range are out.
traps: Using the given angle directly in the cosine rule instead of its supplement at the diagonal's own vertex.
Confusing ∠C (opposite, equal to ∠A) with ∠D (adjacent, supplementary to ∠A).
For the diagonal, forgetting the cosine rule needs the INCLUDED angle between the two known sides.

pyqs.text: The angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 4 : 4. What is the largest angle?
solution: The four angles add to 360°, and the ratio parts add to 1 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 12.
The largest angle = 4 × 30° = 120°. (Strictly, no pairing of these angles gives opposite sums of 180°, so the question only works with the 360° sum.)
pyqs.trick: 360 ÷ 12 = 30, so every angle is a multiple of 30. Only 90° and 120° are, and 90° is the 3-part angle.

a.note: 90° is the angle with 3 parts, not the largest.

b.note: Parts of 30° give multiples of 30°, and 108° is not one.

d.note: Parts of 30° give multiples of 30°, and 135° is not one.

pyqs.text: In a regular polygon, the exterior and interior angles are in the ratio 1 : 4. The number of sides of the polygon is
solution: Exterior + interior = 180°, and they are in the ratio 1 : 4, so exterior = 180° × 1/5 = 36°.
Number of sides = 360° ÷ exterior angle = 360° ÷ 36° = 10.
pyqs.trick: Exterior angle alone decides n = 360/exterior; interior angle is only needed to set up the ratio.

a.note: Used interior angle's share (4/5 of 180° = 144°) as if it were the exterior angle: 360/144 is not even on the list.

c.note: Divided 360° by the ratio sum (1+4=5), not by the exterior angle itself.

d.note: Took exterior angle as 180° × 2/9 by a wrong split of the ratio.

pyqs.text: If the sum of the interior angles of a regular polygon be 1080°, the number of sides of the polygon is
solution: Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°.
pyqs.trick: 1080 ÷ 180 = 6 exactly, so n − 2 = 6 reads off at once.

a.note: Took n − 2 = 1080/180 − 2 = 4, an extra subtraction of 2.

d.note: Divided by 90° instead of 180°, then halved wrongly.

pyqs.text: Measure of each interior angle of a regular polygon can never be:
solution: A regular polygon's interior angle a must give a whole number of sides n = 360/(180 − a), with n ≥ 3.
105° ⟹ n = 360/75 = 4.8, not a whole number — impossible.
pyqs.trick: 180 − a must divide 360 exactly. 180 − 105 = 75, and 75 does not divide 360.

a.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (b) 105°.

c.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (b) 105°.

d.note: Does not match the worked answer, which is option (b) 105°.

pyqs.text: ABCD is a cyclic trapezium such that AD ∥ BC. If ∠ABC = 70°, then the value of ∠BCD is:
solution: A cyclic trapezium is always isosceles (AB = DC), so its base angles at B and C — both touching BC — are equal.
∠BCD = ∠ABC = 70° directly; no further computation is needed.
pyqs.trick: Cyclic + trapezium ⟹ isosceles trapezium, so the two base angles on BC are simply equal — read the answer straight off.

a.note: Guessed a round number instead of using the isosceles-trapezium equal-base-angle rule.

c.note: Computed 180° − 2×70° by a wrong angle-sum attempt.

pyqs.text: ABCD is a cyclic trapezium whose sides AD and BC are parallel to each other. If ∠ABC = 72°, then the measure of ∠BCD is
solution: Same fact as before: AD ∥ BC and ABCD cyclic ⟹ isosceles trapezium ⟹ base angles at B and C are equal.
∠BCD = ∠ABC = 72°.
pyqs.trick: Same shortcut again — the two base angles on BC match, so ∠BCD = ∠ABC.

c.note: 180° − 72° = 108°, treating B and C as the co-interior (supplementary) pair instead of the equal base-angle pair.

pyqs.text: If an exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is 50°, then the interior opposite angle is:
solution: In a cyclic quadrilateral, the exterior angle at a vertex equals the interior angle at the OPPOSITE vertex
(because the interior angle at the same vertex and that opposite interior angle are supplementary, and the exterior angle is also supplementary to the same-vertex interior angle).
So the interior opposite angle = 50°, the same as the exterior angle.
pyqs.trick: Exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral = interior OPPOSITE angle — a direct equality, not a subtraction from 180°.

a.note: 180° − 50°, confusing this with the interior angle at the SAME vertex.

d.note: Unrelated guess of a right angle.

pyqs.text: The ratio of the angles ∠A and ∠B of a non-square rhombus ABCD is 4 : 5, then the value of ∠C is:
solution: Adjacent angles of a rhombus (a parallelogram) are supplementary: ∠A + ∠B = 180°.
Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, so ∠C = ∠A = 80°.
pyqs.trick: ∠C is opposite ∠A, so it equals ∠A — only the ratio split of 180° into 4 : 5 needs computing.

a.note: Took ∠C as the 5-part share instead of the 4-part share: 180×5/9=100, then halved by mistake.

b.note: Divided 180° by the ratio sum (9) alone.

d.note: Used ∠B (the 5-part angle, 100°) scaled down instead of ∠A.

pyqs.text: ABCD is a rhombus whose side AB = 4 cm and ∠ABC = 120°, then the length of diagonal BD is equal to:
solution: Consecutive angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so ∠A = 180° − 120° = 60°.
In triangle ABD, AB = AD = 4 cm (rhombus sides) with the included angle A = 60°.
By the cosine rule, BD² = 4² + 4² − 2·4·4·cos60° = 32 − 16 = 16, so BD = 4 cm.
pyqs.trick: ∠A = 60° makes triangle ABD equilateral (two sides 4 cm with a 60° included angle) — so BD = AB = 4 cm with no cosine rule needed.

a.note: Took BD as a small fraction of AB with no real computation.
